entries.name: American bison
entries.migrates: seasonal movements to forage, salt and water
behaviour: rolls in dust wallows that other species use
bulls smell out cows in rut
herds stampede when panicked, direction led by cows
entries.notes: The keystone grazer of the tallgrass; tens of millions once turned the plains. Calves are the only easy prey for wolves.

entries.name: Pronghorn
entries.migrates: long-distance seasonal migrations in some herds
behaviour: fastest land animal in the Americas, built to outrun an extinct cheetah
cannot jump fences, crawls under them
flares white rump patch as an alarm signal

voxel_model.pattern: white rump patch and neck bands

entries.notes: Second-fastest land mammal alive; antelope-shaped but its own family, and can sustain 55 km/h for kilometres.

entries.name: Mustang (feral horse)
behaviour: harems led by a dominant stallion, plus bachelor bands
feral descendants of released domestic horses
BLM-managed herds on public land
entries.notes: The free-roaming plains horse; management herds gather and adopt out young animals, a ready-made taming mechanic.

entries.name: White-tailed deer
behaviour: flags the white tail underside to warn others
bucks rattle antlers in rut
freezes then bolts when it scents danger
entries.notes: The most common deer of the eastern and prairie plains; its bounding white flag is a readable alarm animation.

entries.name: Pampas deer
behaviour: small, golden-brown native deer of the open pampas grass steppe
haremless browsers, males argue but do not hold groups
spotted fawns hide in grass
entries.notes: The only plains-endemic South American deer and critically endangered; never a routine hunt.

entries.name: Black-tailed prairie dog
behaviour: 'towns' of warrens covering square kilometres, built in coteries of a few families
sentries bark alarm calls specific to predators
trims grass around burrows to spot threats
entries.notes: The keystone engineer: its colonies host bison, ferrets, owls and burrowing life; poison prairie-dog towns and the biome flattens.

entries.name: Thirteen-lined ground squirrel
behaviour: thirteen alternating lines of dots and dashes on the back
hibernates ~6-8 months a year in underground burrows
zig-zags and freezes flat to evade predators
entries.notes: The little striped dart-and-freeze of every farm lawn and prairie edge; model it flickering through grass.

entries.name: Plains pocket gopher
behaviour: lives nearly always underground in root-filled burrow galleries
external fur-lined cheek pouches carry food
pushes up fan-shaped soil mounds that ruin mowing
entries.notes: Mostly invisible: its mounds and the coyote's digging are how the player should meet it.

entries.name: Black-footed ferret
behaviour: obligate prairie-dog predator; sleeps by day in prairie-dog burrows
nearly went extinct; recovered through breeding and reintroduction
does a stiff, bouncing 'war dance'

voxel_model.pattern: black mask, black feet and tail tip

entries.notes: The flagship recovery story of the plains; an endangered treasure found only where prairie dogs still run.

entries.name: Prairie vole
behaviour: monogamous pairs tunnel runways under matted grass
stocks grass nests above and below ground
population outbreaks follow good grass years
entries.notes: Base-prey for the whole raptor guild; a mouse that makes the grass move if you watch closely.

entries.name: Common vole
behaviour: numbers swing on 3-5 year cycles
feeds on field edges, under grain and hay
channel systems link burrows into maze networks
entries.notes: The rodent engine of European meadows; when voles boom, barn owls and harriers raise extra young.

entries.name: American badger
behaviour: digs like a machine; excavates burrows with huge front claws
delayed implantation: mated in summer, young born in spring
co-hunts with coyotes, splitting the digging
entries.notes: The heavy digging forelimbs are the tell; its holes are shelter for kit foxes and burrowing owls after it moves on.

entries.name: Coyote
behaviour: howls at dusk; pairs howl together in chorus
family packs hunt together, loners lope the roads
outsits wolves by being too flexible to exterminate
entries.notes: The trickster of the plains; the animal through whose eyes the player will cross every grassland.

entries.name: Gray wolf
behaviour: packs run down and worry large prey in relay
howls to gather pack and warn rivals
reintroduced to northern plains and Rockies; still recovering
entries.notes: The engine of trophic cascade: wolves back = browsing down = willows up. Heavy mob pressure, handle with care.

entries.name: Red fox
behaviour: pounces ears-first onto voles under snow
caches food in scattered larders
den with many exits in a dirt bank
entries.notes: Everywhere and smart; listens, leaps, caches. The classic 'fox in the field' encounter.

entries.name: Swift fox
behaviour: small pale fox of native shortgrass, follows prairie dogs
dens with multiple exits, easy to snap up
collapsed from poisoning era; slowly reintroduced

voxel_model.pattern: dark nose bar, black tail tip

entries.notes: The pocket-desert fox of the shortgrass; shyer and smaller than the red fox it replaced in parts of its range.

entries.name: Black-tailed jackrabbit
behaviour: huge ears dump heat; bounds 6-7 m to flee coyotes
loosens in open groups, rabbit-like but running, never hiding
browses sagebrush and crop edges at night
entries.notes: The hare of the open west; not a rabbit and does not burrow, so no den crafting here.

entries.name: European hare
behaviour: forms 'leaps' of chasing boxing hares in the March breeding season
lays up in field forms (scrapes) by day
precocial leverets born open-eyed and furless
entries.notes: The farmland hare of Europe; a field that sits silent until something brown explodes out of it.

entries.name: Greater rhea
behaviour: male alone incubates a communal nest of up to 30-80 eggs
zigzag running with wing-sails in high grass
communal flocks of 'ñandú' cross the pampas in lines
entries.notes: The South American ostrich: father-only nesting, flocks to a hundred, and 60 km/h dashes across the estancia grass.

entries.name: Sandhill crane
entries.migrates: spectacular continental migrations; stages by the hundreds of thousands on the Platte River
behaviour: bugling calls carry for kilometres over a valley at dawn
dancing leaps with wings raised in courtship
feeds in wide fields, roosts standing in shallow water
entries.notes: Gestation_days is incubation. The Platte River migration is one of the last great animal spectacles; model the sky full of them.

entries.name: Greater prairie-chicken
behaviour: males boom on communal leks at dawn, inflating orange air sacs and stamping feet
'booming grounds' are traditional for decades
booming audible half a kilometre off

voxel_model.pattern: barred brown and buff, black flank pinnae

entries.notes: The tallgrass's display bird; a lek at dawn is the single most evocative soundscape this biome can offer.

entries.name: Western meadowlark
entries.migrates: short-distance; northern birds move south in winter
behaviour: flute-like song from a fence post is the sound of open country
proud yellow breast with black V
walks rather than hops between foraging spots
entries.notes: Every pasture gate and telephone wire; the quickest way to make a generated plains feel inhabited.

entries.name: Eurasian skylark
entries.migrates: partial migrant; northern populations winter south
behaviour: song pours from a speck suspended almost motionless in the sky
erects small crest when alarmed
declines sharply with intensive farming
entries.notes: The sky-singer of European meadows; an audio landmark, not a visual one -- place the song above empty grass.

entries.name: Bobolink
entries.migrates: long-distance, from South America to North American meadows and back
behaviour: male in breeding plumage is black with a white nape and gold rump -- 'reverse tuxedo'
bubbling song from a bobbing flight over hayfields
old name 'rice bird': followed the wheat belt

voxel_model.pattern: white nape wedges and gold rump on black

entries.notes: A bird animated entirely by flight display: arrange flocks working the timothy and red clover.

entries.name: Grasshopper sparrow
entries.migrates: short-distance; winters in the southern tropics
behaviour: insect-like buzzy song, barely more than a grasshopper's
flattens and hides in grass at the slightest alarm
one of the strongest declines among grassland birds
entries.notes: Invisible grassland specialist; the test of whether your grass and cricket audio systems are doing their job.

entries.name: Burrowing owl
entries.migrates: northern birds migrate south in autumn
behaviour: nests inside prairie-dog and gopher burrows, often in colonies
bobs and 'barleycorn' bowing when nervous
lays scattered feathers and dung at the burrow mouth

voxel_model.pattern: white eyebrows and chin, spotted back

entries.notes: Ground-nesting owl that ties the prairie-dog economy together; pop-up 'periscope' look from a burrow mouth.

entries.name: American kestrel
entries.migrates: partial migrant; northern breeders move south
behaviour: hovers to scan grass, tail spread, then stoops
nests in holes and old woodpecker cavities
tiny falcon with two black facial bars like sideburns

voxel_model.pattern: rufous with two black face stripes, male blue-grey wings

entries.notes: The hovering falcon of roadsides; cheapest iconic raptor to animate -- kestrel-on-a-wire is pure readability.

entries.name: Red-tailed hawk
entries.migrates: partial migrant; northern birds move south in winter
behaviour: broad-winged soaring circles over fields at midday
red tail fans when circling down
the default 'eagle cry' of film sound
entries.notes: The everyman raptor: fence-post sentinel and soaring midday circle. Breaks the 'empty sky' problem in open country.

entries.name: Northern harrier
entries.migrates: partial migrant; most northern birds move south
behaviour: quarters low over grass with wings in a shallow V, ears-tuned to voles
white rump patch is the field mark
formerly called marsh hawk

voxel_model.pattern: white rump patch; male pale grey, female brown

entries.notes: Low V-winged quartering flight is unmistakable; pairs beautifully with vole-run grass and a whisper of wind.

entries.name: Swainson's hawk
entries.migrates: long-distance; gathers in huge thermal kettles, winters in South America
behaviour: migrates in kettles of thousands spiraling upward over Mexico each autumn
light-morph male has rust-red bib
epicure of grasshoppers after cultivation
entries.notes: Construct the migration kettle as a set-piece: a spiral of hawks a kilometre wide over autumn thermals.

entries.name: Common nighthawk
behaviour: nasal 'peent' call at dusk; dives and flexes wings for a booming whoosh
nests on bare gravel roofs and road cuts
long pointed wings with a white half-bar
entries.notes: A crepuscular 'goatsucker' relative; the dusk peent-boom over a gravel roof is a small, perfect plains moment.

entries.name: Killdeer
entries.migrates: partial migrant; northern birds winter south
behaviour: broken-wing display lures predators from the bare-scrape nest
two black breast bands; runs in zigzag spurts
screams its name: kill-deer, kill-deer

voxel_model.pattern: two black breast bands, rufous rump

entries.notes: The open-ground plover of gravel bars and shortgrass; its broken-wing act is a ready-made decoy for the player.

entries.name: Monarch butterfly
entries.migrates: multi-generational relay migration to Mexican oyamel forests
behaviour: larvae eat milkweed; cardenolides make them foul to birds
overwintering monarchs roost in dense orange clusters
navigates by sun compass and inherited relay

voxel_model.pattern: orange with black veins and white-dotted borders

entries.notes: gestation_days is time from egg to caterpillar emergence; adults of the migratory generation live ~8 months. The autumn stream of orange is unmissable.

entries.name: Migratory locust
entries.migrates: swarms with the wind; phase-shifts from solitary hopper to gregarious swarmer
behaviour: touch triggers the solitary-to-crowding phase change
bands of flightless hoppers march and fly
historically devastated plain harvests
entries.notes: Two animals in one skin; the gregaria swarm is an ecological disaster state, not a species trait, and it is terrifying at scale.

entries.name: Plains spadefoot toad
behaviour: explosive breeding in rain pools after rare summer storms
keratin spade on hind foot for digging backwards into soil
tadpoles metamorphose in as little as a week before the puddle dries

voxel_model.pattern: lyre-shaped markings on back, vertical pupils

entries.notes: The plains holds its breath for the storm; one night of chorus and a thousand foaming eggs, then silence for a year.

entries.name: Western rattlesnake
behaviour: rattles a dry warning before striking; rattle counts age in segments
hibernates communally in rock-crevice dens, dozens sharing
ambush sit-and-wait on rodent runs and trail edges

voxel_model.pattern: dark diamond/oval blotches with pale borders

entries.notes: Give dens a real presence: a shared rock fissure the whole snake population pours into in autumn.

entries.name: Gopher snake (bullsnake)
behaviour: mimics rattlesnakes: coils, hisses and vibrates its tail to fake the rattle
constrictor that hunts rodent runs by day
eggs laid in loose soil, 55-70 day incubation
entries.notes: The harmless rattler impersonator; if the player kills every 'rattlesnake' on sight, it will kill its own best rodent control.
